correctness.rationale: The independent chi-square–Dirichlet factorization gives S_n=T²V_n and slope error sigma G/(T sqrt(V_n)); the negative-moment integrals yield all moment cutoffs. Orthogonality of mean Gaussian noise and slope noise establishes conditional unbiasedness and conditional variance; exact chi-square inverse moments give the stated rational factor and sharp gain condition. The 2,748 reproducible checks pass, and the analytic proof treats all n rather than extrapolating from finite tests.

value.rationale: The concrete one-dimensional low-fidelity quadratic benchmark demonstrates an otherwise hidden finite-pilot pathology: a same-sample correction can be unbiased with infinite variance even when every raw observation has all finite moments. The exact \(n=5\) boundary and positive signal-to-noise improvement cutoff are actionable for pilot sizes, regularization and checking multifidelity implementations. This is a motivated structural boundary, not a claim of a new estimator or generic sample-allocation optimum.
